sections.h2: What should a West Seneca seller know about the town?
sections.html:
West Seneca is a built-out Buffalo suburb, so condition and paperwork drive a sale's timeline more than land does. The town sits in the middle of Erie County, with Buffalo and Lackawanna to the west, Cheektowaga to the north, Orchard Park to the south and Elma and Lancaster to the east. It covers 21.4 square miles and had 45,500 residents in 2020.

West Seneca, Orchard Park and Hamburg together make up the inner Southtowns. The land was part of the Buffalo Creek Reservation, so it opened to European settlement only in the mid-19th century. The Town of Seneca formed in 1851 from parts of Cheektowaga and Hamburg, and it became West Seneca in 1852. Lackawanna split off in 1909. The population peaked near 51,210 in 1980 and has hovered around 45,000 since 2000.

sections.h2: Which parts of West Seneca do buyers ask about?
sections.html:
Named areas include Gardenville and New Ebenezer in the north, East Seneca along Route 16, and Ebenezer in the center, which takes its name from a German religious community that settled around 1843. Cazenovia Creek and Buffalo Creek run through the town.

Roads matter to buyers here. The New York State Thruway (I-90) crosses the western part of town and meets NY 400, the Aurora Expressway, and U.S. 219 reaches the southwest corner. NY 16 (Seneca Street and Center Road) and NY 354 (Clinton Street) run east and west, while NY 240, NY 277 (Union Road) and Transit Road (NY 78) run north and south.

  • Northern streets near Gardenville: close to Cheektowaga and Buffalo.
  • Central Ebenezer and Union Road: near Town Hall.
  • Along Route 16 and NY 400: quick access to the expressway.
  • Southern streets near Orchard Park: edges of the Orchard Park school district.

sections.h2: Which school district serves a West Seneca address?
sections.html:
Three public districts operate inside the town. The West Seneca Central School District is the largest and covers most of it, but parts of the town lie in the Orchard Park Central School District and the Cheektowaga-Sloan Union Free School District. Confirm which district a parcel belongs to before you advertise it, since school taxes arrive on a separate bill.

Private options inside the town include Queen of Heaven School, St. John Vianney School, Trinity Christian School, West Seneca Christian School and the Center Road Christian Academy. The Charles E. Burchfield Nature and Art Center, a 29-acre site along Buffalo Creek, is one of the local landmarks.

Two sites in town are on the National Register of Historic Places: the Eaton Site, listed in 1979, and the Community of True Inspiration Residence, listed in 2013. The Buffalo Airfield, a general aviation airport, sits on the north town line.

sections.h2: How is transfer tax figured on a West Seneca sale?
sections.html:
Erie County adds a local transfer tax to the state's, which makes a West Seneca seller's bill larger than a seller's in a county that only charges the state rate. According to the Erie County Clerk the combined rate is $4.50 for every $500 of price, made up of $2.00 for the state and $2.50 for the county. The price is rounded up to the next $500, the seller is responsible, and the money goes in at the clerk's counter along with the deed.

The clerk's own illustration is a $104,501 house, which owes $420 to the state and $525 to the county, for $945. Following the same method, a $200,000 sale is 400 units of $500 and owes $1,800. A seller who is 62 or older and has owned and lived in a one- or two-family house for at least a year can claim the lower $2.00 rate by filing an affidavit with the clerk.

Separately, the buyer pays a 1 percent mansion tax on residential sales of $1 million or more.

sections.h2: What does recording a West Seneca deed cost at the Erie County Clerk?
sections.html:
The clerk's fee schedule is short, and its own worked example for a three-page residential deed comes to $195. Payment can be cash, check, money order, cashier's check or a Visa, MasterCard or Discover card.

The transfer tax described above is paid on top of these fees.

sections.h2: How do West Seneca property taxes and exemptions work?
sections.html:
Assessments are handled in Room 211 of Town Hall at 1250 Union Road, and the Town Clerk collects taxes as Receiver from Room 212 down the hall. Town and county bills arrive in mid-January and carry a February 15 due date, after which a penalty applies. School bills arrive in mid-September and carry an October 15 due date. The town hands unpaid town and county taxes to Erie County on July 1 and unpaid school taxes on December 1.

Partial payments are accepted in the office. Credit card payments carry a convenience fee of 2.45 percent, and e-checks carry a $1.75 fee. The town discourages bank bill pay because those mailings lack a U.S. postmark. Check the current bill, since due dates and fees are set each year.

Exemption applications for the 2027 roll are due by March 1, 2027. The town lists a senior citizens exemption that can trim an assessment by 5 to 50 percent, open to homeowners aged 65 and up whose combined income is under $37,400, and a similar exemption for people with disabilities and limited income below $32,400. The state now runs the STAR program directly, and the town no longer accepts STAR applications. Veterans may qualify for 15 percent of assessed value, up to $18,000, with added amounts for combat service and disability.

sections.h2: What local rules affect a West Seneca house before closing?
sections.html:
The Code Enforcement Office issues building, plumbing and electrical permits and carries out inspections, and the town says no inspection happens without a house number and a permit. A certificate of code compliance is issued only after the required inspections pass. If a deck, finished basement or addition was built without paperwork, ask the office how to close it out.

West Seneca also adopted an ordinance requiring owners of rental properties to register with the Town Clerk's Office by filing a Rental Housing Business License Application. For a house that has had tenants, check that the registration is current and tell the buyer. The Code Enforcement Office can answer questions at 716-558-3242.

A cash buyer is an option when a house has open permits, a rental past or deferred repairs, since no appraisal stands in the way. Judge every offer by what you net after transfer tax, payoff and tax adjustments.

faqs.q: What is the transfer tax on a West Seneca home sale?
faqs.a: It is $4.50 per $500 of the price, made up of $2.00 for New York State and $2.50 for Erie County. The seller pays at recording, so a $300,000 sale is 600 units of $500 and owes $2,700.

faqs.q: Do West Seneca seniors get a lower transfer tax rate?
faqs.a: Yes. A seller aged 62 or older who owned and lived in a one- or two-family house for at least a year can pay $2.00 per $500 instead of $4.50. The Erie County Clerk provides the affidavit at no charge.

faqs.q: Which dates matter on a West Seneca tax bill?
faqs.a: February 15 for town and county taxes, with bills mailed in mid-January, and October 15 for school taxes. Town and county balances move to Erie County on July 1, and school balances move on December 1.

faqs.q: Must a rental house be registered with the town before it is sold?
faqs.a: The town requires rental property owners to register with the Town Clerk's Office through a Rental Housing Business License Application. If the house has been rented, confirm the registration is current before you sell.

faqs.q: Where do West Seneca owners apply for tax exemptions?
faqs.a: At the Assessor's Office, 1250 Union Road, Room 211. Applications for the 2027 roll are due March 1, 2027, and STAR is now run by the state, so contact the New York State Tax Department for that program.
